private_note: Cedar puts my household at 76, the most on offer. Alder and Today both leave me at 72, but Alder guarantees a minimum income and health coverage. As a self-employed driver still paying off a truck, that protects me if I get hurt or freight dries up, so Alder beats Today. Birch at 68 and Hazel at 64 cost me real money. Cedar probably can't reach nine votes, so Alder is my realistic target, and I'd rather have it than fail.
statement: I drive a truck I'm still paying off, and I run my own small business on the road. I'm in the middle, and I'll stay there whatever we pick, so I'm looking at the middle column. Cedar gives my family the most, and I'm ranking it first. Birch and Hazel would take money out of my house to level things off, and I can't support that. Here's the practical point: we need nine of twelve, and if we fail we're stuck with today for a generation. Alder leaves the middle exactly where it is. It raises the bottom two groups, costs the top groups only a little, and gives everyone a floor on income and health coverage. For self-employed people like me, that floor is worth something. If Cedar can't get to nine, I'm ready to back Alder. I'd like to hear from anyone at the top on whether they could live with it.
